cards.issue_title: Government charges look the same on every bank, and the card repeats the table
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks → Charges, every lender shows the same government-charges rupee figure.
Opening a bank’s card shows CERSAI, MODT stamp duty, NOI filing, and NOI registration — the same stack for each bank.
The notes under the table say those figures again, so it is hard to tell what is unique to a bank versus what is just Maharashtra / India tax.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Charges, they treated government charges as the same number on every bank, with stamp duty and NOI explained twice — once in the table/notes and again in the side card — so a user cannot tell bank-specific fees from Maharashtra/India government fees.
cards.on_screen_object: Charges tab → Government charges column (₹30,518 on every bank) + government-charges drawer (CERSAI / MODT stamp duty / NOI filing / NOI registration) + Notes → Government charges (^)
quotes_sample: This is the same. You have the same screen information in the same card.
How would you know if the information is in the card?
It is not a problem. It is time duty.
related_discussion_one_liners: Numbered 1–4–5 cards in the drawer continue the previous recording’s talk that sequential charge cards should "flow".
SBI property-check ₹15,100 was opened first as a neighbouring charge card, then they moved to government charges.
Stamp duty + registration treated as "not a problem" as real government items, but still a presentation problem.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Charges-tab government-charges column showing the same ₹30,518 stack on every bank and repeating it in notes and the side card — not rate-change jargon and not overdue % without a rupee calculation.

cards.issue_title: Rate-change charges are too complex and read like legal jargon, not advice
summary_4_lines: On Explore banks → Other charges, the Rate change charge column has a dropdown: Floating → Fixed, Repricing, Benchmark switch.
They said there are too many complexes, then walked MCLR, repo, LIBOR/MIBOR, and CIBIL bargaining.
They asked for three or four plain ways banks set rates, in the voice of a lawyer’s advice, not technical terms.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Other charges, the Rate change charge column and its type dropdown plus the ° notes are too complex (MCLR, repo, many symbols); they wanted a short lawyer-like explanation of the few ways banks set rates, not legal/technical words.
cards.on_screen_object: Other charges tab → Rate change charge column + Rate change type combobox (Floating → Fixed / Repricing / Benchmark switch / Type switch) + Notes ° for rate-change charge
quotes_sample: Oh my god! There are many complexes.
This needs to be a lot simpler.
Should feel like an advice coming from a lawyer instead of just technical terms and legal words.
related_discussion_one_liners: CIBIL as bargaining power to force a rate change; floating→fixed described as the simple case.
Repo as something that does not auto-change for the borrower.
MCLR full form and who decides it; LIBOR/MIBOR/IBA as other benchmarks.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the Other-charges Rate change charge dropdown and ° notes being too complex and legal — not government charges looking identical across banks, and not overdue % p.a. without a rupee walkthrough.

cards.issue_title: Overdue charge shows a yearly percent with no rupee calculation for a missed EMI
summary_4_lines: On Other charges, overdue is written as 2% p.a., 5% p.a., 8% p.a.
They asked what 5% means in money after one missed EMI, how overdue is made, when a notice goes, and when a collection agency comes.
They said 2% per annum is the wrong unit if the borrower only missed the next month.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Other charges, overdue is only a percent per annum with no calculation of rupees after one missed EMI, no notice timeline, and no collection-agency timeline — they said that is not usable.
cards.on_screen_object: Other charges tab → Overdue charge column (‡) and its note; cells such as 2.00% p.a. / 5.00% p.a. / 8.00% p.a.
quotes_sample: How did you get 2%? You have written the annum. But I put a total amount in the next month. I have not used the money for an annum.
related_discussion_one_liners: Listed the questions a borrower would ask after missing an EMI (how overdue is made, how much money/charge, days until notice, days until a collection agency).
"Monitoring value" / putting data on top of the calculation: they want inputs (EMI missed, days late) driving a shown sum.
EMI bounce is on the same table but they did not attack bounce as a separate defect here; next recording folds bounce into the same overdue-calculation drawer.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is overdue shown only as % per annum with no rupee calculation, notice days, or collection-agency days after one missed EMI — not duplicated government charges and not rate-change legal jargon.
